summary.text: Davydd Griffiths, a City of Melbourne councillor since 2020, is Labor's candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. He led Labor's councillor ticket at the 2020 and 2024 council elections and won a seat both times. His earlier work includes teaching, advising on education and health policy, and owning hospitality venues in the city's west; the ABC says he arrived in Melbourne in 1993.

occupation.text: Former teacher and small business owner

prior_roles.role: Owner of hospitality venues in Melbourne's west

priorities.text: Support for renters
High-quality health care
Better public schools

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Ellen Sandell has been the Greens member for Melbourne since 2014, when she became the first Green to win a seat in Victoria's lower house. She has led the Victorian Greens since April 2024, after years as the party's deputy leader. Before Parliament she headed the Australian Youth Climate Coalition and advised the state government on climate policy. She is recontesting Melbourne in 2026.

occupation.text: Climate campaigner (head of the Australian Youth Climate Coalition) and government climate policy adviser; trained in science

prior_roles.role: Deputy Leader of the Victorian Greens
prior_roles.note: Wikipedia dates this from December 2018; the Parliament of Victoria page lists it from February 2023.

prior_roles.role: Acting Leader of the Victorian Greens
Manager of Greens Business in the Legislative Assembly
Greens spokesperson for climate change and the environment
Campaign manager for Simon Sheikh's Senate campaign

previous_candidacies.note: Parliament of Victoria lists her service as continuous since 2014; neither source describes this election.

priorities.text: Moving Victoria from coal and gas to renewable energy
Ending native forest logging
Public housing and housing affordability
Support for the arts
Keeping Melbourne liveable

sources.title: Ellen Sandell, Parliament of Victoria
Ellen Sandell, Wikipedia

summary.text: Jordan van den Lamb, a housing activist known online as Purple Pingers, is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. His videos exposing poor rental conditions drew wide attention, and he runs shitrentals.org, a site where tenants report bad rentals. He led the party's Victorian Senate ticket at the 2025 federal election; he studied law and now works in the public service, where he serves as a delegate for the Community and Public Sector Union.

previous_candidacies.note: First on the Victorian Socialists Senate ticket, which won 1.5% of the vote.

priorities.text: Taking action against owners who leave homes empty or rent out unsafe, overpriced housing
Cutting politicians' salaries and taxing the very wealthy to fund housing, schools, hospitals and transport
Ending the extra votes businesses and landlords get in City of Melbourne elections
Defending bulk-billed health care and public institutions such as the State Library

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jordan van den Lamb, Victorian Socialists
Jordan van den Lamb, Wikipedia
Candidates of the 2025 Australian federal election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Matthew Collins is One Nation's candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. His ABC listing gives just two facts: a career in sales, and a small business of his own locally that he describes as successful. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile, and no other biography had been published as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Naomi Jones is standing for the Animal Justice Party in Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. She holds a master's degree in design communication and diplomas in interior design and dental technology. Once a graphic and interior designer, she is now a dental technician and the director and practice manager of a dental practice, and is studying law at Deakin University. Her party page says she has volunteered with animal rescue groups for about 30 years and has also helped people who are homeless.

occupation.text: Dental technician, practice manager and director of a dental practice

priorities.text: Stronger animal protection laws, covering breeding, racing, farming, testing, fur and wildlife
Continued government funding for supported accommodation services for people experiencing homelessness
Practical support for people affected by domestic violence and for their pets
Better access, cycling infrastructure and traffic flow in and around the CBD

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Naomi Jones for Melbourne, Animal Justice Party Victoria

summary.text: Phillip Courtis is One Nation's candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. His party page says he is 32, a father of two and the youngest of ten children, and that he set up his own care-support business after looking after his father, who was left quadriplegic by an accident. A Phillip Courtis stood for the Trumpet of Patriots in the federal seat of Casey in 2025; no source confirms it is the same person.

prior_roles.role: Founder of a care-industry support service

previous_candidacies.note: Stood for Trumpet of Patriots. Matched by name only: no source says the 2026 candidate is the Casey candidate.

priorities.text: Restoring safety, prosperity and trust in Melbourne
Returning transparency and respect to the Victorian Parliament
Advocacy for people in the care industry

sources.title: Candidates for Melbourne District, Victorian Electoral Commission
Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Rafael Camillo is the Liberal candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from Brazil, he came to Melbourne as an international student close to 20 years ago and has lived in the CBD for many years. He chaired the residents' group Residents 3000 before winning a City of Melbourne council seat in 2024, where he heads the safety and cleaning portfolio.

prior_roles.role: Portfolio lead, safety and cleaning; deputy portfolio lead, infrastructure

previous_candidacies.note: Headed the Team Morgan councillor ticket.

priorities.text: A safer city with less crime
Lower living costs
Speaking up for the city's residents and traders

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Rafael Camillo, Liberal for Melbourne, Liberal Victoria
2024 Melbourne City Council election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Rob McCathie is the Libertarian candidate for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election and is the party's registered officer with the Victorian Electoral Commission. He has worked in IT for his whole career, administering computer systems and consulting for small and medium businesses. At the 2022 state election he stood for the upper house in Eastern Victoria Region for the Liberal Democrats, the party's former name. The party's own 2026 candidates page did not list him as at early November.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Rob McCathie second on the Liberal Democrats ticket, which won no seat; the ABC says he has stood three times before but names only 2022, so this match is by name and party.
Wikipedia lists a Rob McCathie as the Liberal Democrats candidate (2.1% of the primary vote); no source we read confirms it is the same person.
First on the Liberal Democrats ticket, which won no seat in the region.

Wikipedia lists a Rob McCathie as the Libertarian candidate (1.2% of the primary vote); no source we read confirms it is the same person. With this one, Wikipedia's lists give four earlier candidacies, where the ABC says three.

summary.text: Rowan Tuckfield is running as an independent for Melbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. An economics graduate who majored in accounting, he spent about 20 years in finance and served on the Premier's Infrastructure Planning Council late in the 1990s. He later lived in New York for 17 years, where he ran a coffee business, and says he is funding his campaign himself without donations.

prior_roles.role: Independent financial expert, State Water Policy White Paper
Owner of a coffee business in New York
Lender to refugee-owned small businesses at a not-for-profit

priorities.text: I want our $15 billion back and the people responsible punished.
Halting demolition of public housing towers, phasing out Airbnb-style short stays and offering five-year leases
Reassessing the Suburban Rail Loop and dropping the Airport Rail Link
Help with insurance and rent for live music venues and historic pubs
Public reporting of how many police are on frontline duty

sources.title: Melbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
